test_command.description: The test command run. Written as a bare string by some runs and as an object ({command, exit_code, …}) by others, so both are accepted — this artifact is an evidence document the orchestrator shapes per run, not a fixed record.

story.description: Repo-relative path to the story. Optional: the test-scope edge needs it to resolve AC priorities and reports an honest no-op without it, rather than the artifact being invalid.

mutation.description: The mutation gate's result: the diff's own production lines broken on purpose, and whether the diff's tests noticed. `ran: false` carries a `reason` and is never an empty pass — a gate that did not run must not read as a clean one. When `ran` is true, `survived[]` is the finding: each entry is a line this branch changed that no test defends.

capped.description: True when the mutant budget cut the candidate list, so `killed/mutants` is a sample rather than the whole diff.

tests.description: Optional. When present, `covers` is what lets the scope edge check P0/P1 in both directions; without it the edge no-ops.

_shape_note: Deliberately OPEN. Across the eight verify.json written before this schema existed, only `item` appears in every one, and `test_command` appears in two different types. The artifact is a free-form evidence document — `gates`, `discrepancies`, `planned_vs_realized`, `coverage_percent` and 80 other keys vary by run. A closed schema rejected all eight and blocked their edges, which is why this requires the one stable field and validates the shapes it can rather than inventing a contract the step never had.
